LESSON: READING FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.1: Reading Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you ensure fluency in reading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text on formal greetings and introduction
2. apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING FLUENCY
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Fluency helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a text on formal greetings and introduction

What this means
In this part you learn to read a text on formal greetings and introduction. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a text on formal greetings and introduction.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a text on formal greetings and introduction. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Fluency to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a text on formal greetings and introduction)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Fluency to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a text on formal greetings and introduction.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you ensure fluency in reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a text on formal greetings and introduction.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
